evidence: All 9 tools use the geo_* snake_case prefix (server.py @mcp.tool names: geo_search_layers, geo_identify, geo_find, geo_municipality_at, geo_zoning_at, geo_height, geo_elevation_profile, geo_layer_info, geo_convert_coordinates)
Every tool docstring states the use case and the upstream data source, e.g. server.py geo_zoning_at: 'Harmonised building zone(s) at an LV95 point ... Data source: ch.are.bauzonen'
Empty upstream results are returned as an explicit soft-miss note rather than a bare empty payload, e.g. server.py geo_identify note 'No feature at this point on the given layer (soft miss).'
Server logic is transport-agnostic: tools are defined on the FastMCP instance in server.py; __main__.py selects stdio/streamable-http/sse via SWISS_GEODATA_TRANSPORT and calls mcp.run(transport=...)
No secrets in the codebase; the server needs no credentials (geo.admin.ch is public). grep for keys/tokens over src/ is empty.
9 high-level, use-case-oriented tools over ~700 layers via a discovery entry point (geo_search_layers) rather than one tool per layer/endpoint
Tools are atomic at the boundary (one point/feature query each); composition (e.g. municipality current-year filter) is internal to the tool
Tools primitive fully used (9 @mcp.tool)
gaps: No MCP Resources or Prompts are exposed (grep '@mcp.resource'/'@mcp.prompt' over src/ is empty). Layer catalogue / layer metadata would be natural Resources; consistent with the portfolio's tools-only convention.

evidence: All tools carry annotations readOnlyHint=True, destructiveHint=False, idempotentHint=False, openWorldHint=True via the shared _READ_ONLY dict (server.py:134)
src-layout (src/swiss_geodata_mcp/), tests/, README.md + README.de.md, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE, pyproject.toml all present
CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog + SemVer; pyproject pins mcp[cli]>=1.28.1,<2.0.0 (upper bound guards against SDK 2.x breakage)
Every response carries the upstream 'source' (GeoEnvelope, models.py); README License section attributes geo.admin.ch/swisstopo/ARE as OGD with attribution
Errors are surfaced to the model via _handle_error (server.py:116) as user-facing strings; FastMCP wraps string returns into the MCP envelope
gaps: Tools return sanitised error strings rather than an explicit isError execution-error envelope. No behavioural impact for the client; documented as accepted risk (same posture as swiss-snb-mcp).

evidence: _handle_error (server.py:116) returns generic messages and logs full detail to stderr only via logger.exception; upstream bodies/stack traces never reach the model
logging.basicConfig(stream=sys.stderr, level=INFO, ...) in server.py:34
gaps: Logs are plain text, not JSON-structured with RFC 5424 severities/trace IDs. Not justified for a stdio server; accepted risk, revisit on cloud/SSE deployment.

evidence: Logging is pinned to stderr (server.py:34-38 basicConfig stream=sys.stderr); stdout is reserved for the JSON-RPC stream on stdio transport
tests/test_unit.py: respx-mocked unit suite (CI-safe); tests/test_live.py: gated with pytest.mark.live; pyproject registers the 'live' marker and CI runs live nightly only
Bilingual README.md + README.de.md; 'Known limitations' section present; 'Project structure' ASCII block; EXAMPLES.md with use cases
Read-only phase-1 only: all 9 tools query upstream; no write/mutating tools (readOnlyHint=True across the board)
Server holds no per-session state (one shared httpx.AsyncClient via lifespan; each tool call is independent), so streamable-http/SSE can be load-balanced without sticky sessions
gaps: No live cloud/LB deployment exists (deployment=[local-stdio]); statelessness makes sticky-LB moot rather than implemented.

evidence: Egress is an HTTPS-only allow-list of two fixed public hosts (geoadmin.py:26-30 API_BASE/REFRAME_BASE https + ALLOWED_HOSTS); _assert_host_allowed (geoadmin.py:49) rejects any other host before every request. An allow-list of known public hosts is stronger than IP blocklisting.
Host allow-list restricts egress to api3.geo.admin.ch / geodesy.geo.admin.ch
gaps: No explicit DNS-pinning against TOCTOU rebinding. Low risk: the two allow-listed hosts are fixed public swisstopo endpoints, not user-controlled. Accepted risk for this profile.

evidence: stdio is the default transport (__main__.py: SWISS_GEODATA_TRANSPORT defaults to 'stdio'); network transports are explicit opt-in
Local stdio public-data server; no privileged operations
gaps: No Dockerfile / sandbox. Accepted risk for a local-stdio public-data server; ship a hardened image if the deployment profile ever moves to the cloud (documented in SECURITY.md).

evidence: Install is via uvx/pip with the documented claude_desktop_config snippet
gaps: No formal pre-configuration consent gate. Low impact for a read-only public-data server; accepted risk.

evidence: Server is stateless with no session identifiers to bind (no auth, no sessions); the confused-deputy/session-binding surface does not exist for this profile
No API keys or credentials anywhere — geo.admin.ch is fully public, so there is nothing to store or leak

HTTP transports bind to loopback by default: host=os.getenv('HOST', '127.0.0.1') (server.py:110). Exposing all interfaces requires an explicit HOST=0.0.0.0 opt-in. Fixed in this audit run (was previously defaulting to 0.0.0.0).

Every tool input is a Pydantic v2 model with extra='forbid' and Field constraints (min_length, ge/le); LV95 coordinates are additionally plausibility-checked (_lv95_error, server.py:50) with a pointer to geo_convert_coordinates
gaps: Models do not set strict=True. Deliberate: coordinate fields are float and strict mode would reject integer LV95 inputs from clients. Validation is present and enforced; strict-mode is a possible future tightening if coord fields are typed int|float.

evidence: Read-only server: no write, no send/exfiltration tools. The lethal-trifecta cannot form; register writes live in a separate server (swiss-housing-mcp) by design (README Known limitations)
No os.system / subprocess / shell=True / eval / exec anywhere in src/ (grep empty). All upstream access is via httpx with structured params.

Code-layer egress allow-list enforced by _assert_host_allowed before every outbound GET (geoadmin.py:49, called in _get geoadmin.py:80). Network-layer egress firewalling is a deployment concern, N/A for local stdio.
